content: Before using foscarnet, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This medication may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Foscarnet may cause dizziness. Consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities that require alertness until you are certain you can perform them safely. Limit your intake of alcoholic beverages. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if absolutely necessary. It is not known whether foscarnet passes into breast milk. Due to potential risks to the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, if someone exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. This medication is typically administered in a hospital setting where your condition can be closely monitored. Laboratory and medical tests, such as kidney function, electrolyte levels, complete blood count, and regular eye exams, should be conducted while you are using this medication. Ensure you attend all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist immediately to establish a new dosing schedule. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and heat, and below 104°F (40°C). Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Foscarnet may cause serious side effects, including kidney problems and seizures due to mineral or electrolyte imbalances. You may be given fluids and/or minerals/electrolytes while receiving this medication. Your doctor should monitor your kidney function and perform lab tests to minimize the risk of these side effects. This medication is used to manage cytomegalovirus (CMV) eye infections (CMV retinitis) in individuals with AIDS. It is an antiviral that works by inhibiting the growth of viruses. Controlling CMV retinitis can help reduce the risk of blindness caused by the infection. Foscarnet is administered via injection into a vein by a healthcare professional. It is typically given 2 to 3 times daily for the first 2 to 3 weeks of treatment, followed by once daily thereafter. The medication is usually infused slowly over 1 to 2 hours using an infusion pump. If you are using this medication at home, ensure you learn all preparation and usage instructions from your healthcare professional. Do not mix this product with other medications. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration. To prevent kidney damage, it is important to drink plenty of fluids while using this medication. Antivirals are most effective when the medication level in your body remains constant. It is crucial to use this medication exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Do not use more of this drug or infuse it more frequently or faster than directed. If skin contact with this drug occurs, rinse thoroughly with water. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, headache, diarrhea, dizziness, or swelling/pain at the injection site. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Always seek complete information about this product and your specific health needs from your healthcare professional.
